oracle.command: kubectl --context kind-fathom-oracle apply --dry-run=server -f <objectFile> (default --validate=strict unless noted); serverError is kubectl's stderr verbatim

scenarios.name: cel-fail
scenarios.serverError:
The Widget "cel-fail" is invalid: 
* spec: Invalid value: replicas must not exceed maxReplicas
* spec.name: Invalid value: "UPPER": name must be lowercase, got UPPER
scenarios.notes: Violates the object-level rule (replicas 5 > maxReplicas 3, static message) and the field-level rule (spec.name UPPER, messageExpression). Both errors reported in one response.

scenarios.name: cel-pass
scenarios.notes: Same CRD, object satisfies both rules; stderr empty.

scenarios.name: structural
scenarios.serverError: Error from server (BadRequest): error when creating "objects/structural.yaml": Widget in version "v1" cannot be handled as a Widget: strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.colour"
scenarios.notes: Unknown field spec.colour plus spec.replicas as string. kubectl apply default --validate=strict sends fieldValidation=Strict; the server rejects on the unknown field (BadRequest, strict decoding) before schema validation, so the type error is not reported here.

scenarios.name: structural-ignore
scenarios.serverError:
The Widget "structural" is invalid: 
* spec.replicas: Invalid value: "string": spec.replicas in body must be of type integer: "string"
* <nil>: Invalid value: null: some validation rules were not checked because the object was invalid; correct the existing errors to complete validation
scenarios.notes: Same object with --validate=ignore (fieldValidation=Ignore): the server prunes spec.colour silently and reports the type error; type errors are blocking so CEL rules are skipped ('some validation rules were not checked'). --validate=warn gives this same error text plus a 'Warning: unknown field "spec.colour"' line.

scenarios.name: structural-type
scenarios.serverError:
The Widget "structural-type" is invalid: 
* spec.replicas: Invalid value: "string": spec.replicas in body must be of type integer: "string"
* <nil>: Invalid value: null: some validation rules were not checked because the object was invalid; correct the existing errors to complete validation
scenarios.notes: Wrong type only (spec.replicas: "two"), default strict validation. Shows the type-error wording and the blocking-error note that CEL was skipped.

scenarios.name: ratcheting-replicas
scenarios.serverError: Warning: spec.name: Invalid value: "UPPER": name must be lowercase
scenarios.notes: Object created for real under crds/gadget-a.yaml (no rule) with spec.name UPPER; then crds/gadget-b.yaml added `self == self.lowerAscii()` on the same served version. Dry-run update changing only spec.replicas 1->2 is ACCEPTED: CRD validation ratcheting keeps the unchanged invalid spec.name. stderr is a Warning line, not an error. oldObjectFile is the stored object from kubectl get -o yaml (resourceVersion/uid are cluster-specific).

scenarios.name: ratcheting-name
scenarios.serverError: The Gadget "ratchet" is invalid: spec.name: Invalid value: "OTHER": name must be lowercase
scenarios.notes: Dry-run update that changes spec.name UPPER->OTHER (another violating value): not ratcheted, rejected.

scenarios.name: budget
scenarios.serverError: The Blob "budget" is invalid: spec: Invalid value: "object": validation failed due to running out of cost budget, no further validation rules will be run
scenarios.notes: 14 identical rules `self.values.all(x, self.values.all(y, x + y >= 0))` over an integer list with maxItems 350; the object has 350 items. Static estimate per rule is far below the 10,000,000 per-rule limit and the schema total below 100,000,000, but each rule costs between 833,334 and 909,090 at runtime (11 rules pass, 12 already exhaust; 1 rule passes, so the per-call 1,000,000 limit is not hit), so the 10,000,000 per-object RuntimeCELCostBudget runs out and the server reports the exact 1.37 wording. String-based shapes fail at CRD creation because the estimator counts 4 bytes per character (matches() estimated at 16x runtime).
